title: German youth movement stages nationwide protests over living costs and education
seoTitle: Berlin youth protests over living costs

tea.why: Youth are protesting against high living costs, underfunded schools and universities, environmental issues, and potential military service.
tea.want: They demand attention to youth priorities, including education spending, housing improvements, and reduced financial burdens.
tea.changed: Nov 2: Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for a hard stance against rioters, while the movement announced new demonstrations for November 14.

summary: Tens of thousands of participants joined demonstrations across major German cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt, Cologne, and Hamburg, organized by the youth movement 'GenZ regelt!'. The actions coincided with Halloween to maximize visibility, with participants demanding attention to underfunded education, high living costs, environmental concerns, and a potential return of mandatory military service. While most participants demonstrated peacefully, clashes, vandalism, and looting broke out on the sidelines in several cities, including Frankfurt and Cologne, where police deployed water cannons. Government officials, including Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, condemned the violence and pledged a strict legal response, while acknowledging the legitimacy of the peaceful protesters' concerns. The movement announced further demonstrations scheduled for November 14.
demands: Address the high cost of living
Increase funding for schools and universities
Oppose the potential reintroduction of mandatory military service
response: Chancellor Friedrich Merz and other politicians condemned the violence and property destruction while acknowledging the legitimacy of the youth's concerns. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt blamed the unrest on leftist groups and migrant communities.

arrests.text: investigating 54 people in Frankfurt and placed an 18-year-old in custody

injuries.text: More than 100 police officers were injured

updates.text: Youth movement 'GenZ regelt!' staged nationwide demonstrations in cities including Berlin, Frankfurt, Cologne, and Hamburg.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz condemned the sideline clashes and promised a strict response against rioters, while addressing youth concerns.
Organizers announced that the protests were only the start and called for fresh demonstrations on November 14.
